title: Counter with Evidence! A Multi-Agent Memory Efficient Reasoning Framework for Hate Category Informed Counterspeech Generation
measurement_description: The paper measures the effectiveness of various Large Language Models in generating factually grounded, category-informed counterspeech against online hate speech. This includes evaluating the models' ability to neutralize hate speech targeted at specific religious groups (such as Muslims and Jews) by debunking religious stereotypes and conspiracy theories with verifiable facts rather than passive or neutral rebuttals.
findings: The study found that the proposed multi-agent framework (FIRE) successfully identified and neutralized hate speech targeted at religious communities by providing concrete counter-evidence. For example, when confronted with the anti-Muslim statement 'No muslims are compatible with any Western society', baseline models provided hedged rebuttals that inadvertently validated the stereotype by implying conditional legitimacy. In contrast, FIRE directly invalidated the universal generalization by citing the real-world example of London Mayor Sadiq Khan. FIRE also effectively debunked anti-Semitic conspiracy theories regarding global financial control by recognizing the underlying hateful intent and refuting it with demographic and historical facts.
